summary: Democrat Laura Kelly could not run again, so Kansas elected a new governor. Democrat Cindy Holscher won, beating Republican Ty Masterson by less than 1 percentage point.

candidates.name: Cindy Holscher
candidates.bio: Cindy Holscher is an Overland Park Democrat who has served in the Kansas Senate since 2021 and was a state representative for four years before that. She worked for many years at Sprint.

positions.summary: Supports lowering the residential property assessment rate by 2.5% without a hard cap, which would require a constitutional amendment.
Says she will push to fully fund special education as specified in Kansas law, which she says would ease the property tax burden on school districts.
Says she will expand Medicaid and protect rural hospitals.
Says Kansas should stop approving new data centers until guardrails are in place.
Says voters settled the abortion question in 2022 and that she would oppose efforts to restrict reproductive care.
Says she supports enforcing immigration laws but wants federal agents held accountable and ICE reformed.

candidates.name: Ty Masterson
candidates.bio: Ty Masterson is an Andover Republican who served in the Kansas House from 2005 to 2009 and has been a state senator since, serving as Senate president since 2021. He won the Republican primary with President Trump's endorsement.

positions.summary: Says additional property tax relief is his top issue and supports capping annual growth in assessed property valuation at 3% or less through a constitutional amendment.
Says abortion is not a settled issue and that people want fewer abortions.
Says he backs stronger border security and deportations.
Says he opposes Medicaid expansion for able-bodied adults.
Says he wants parents to have a say in their children's education and supports open enrollment.

factCheckNote: Called as of 2026-11-14.
